svg.title: Spaceflight and extreme-environment relevance map
svg.desc: A research map connecting spaceflight hazards to cognition, neurobehavioral performance, measurable physical variables, and consciousness-relevant research questions without treating spaceflight studies as evidence for a consciousness bridge. svg.text: NASA human-performance research provides demanding stress tests for cognition and state monitoring.
Its role here is application and validation, not a consciousness bridge theory.
They can test whether proposed physical
1. Do response fingerprints remain stable under altered gravity?
2. Which temporal changes exceed measurement uncertainty?
3. Can causal markers separate vigilance loss from deeper state change?
4. Which markers are environment-sensitive or robust?
5. Can monitoring avoid confusing fatigue with consciousness change?
state change → model comparison → falsifiable interpretation
NASA HRP: integrated human health and performance research.
HFBP: sleep, cognition, team performance, human-system interaction.
Behavioral-health evidence: cognition under exploration hazards.
Sleep/circadian risk: alertness, fatigue, and performance.
ARCHeR: activity, sleep, well-being, and behavioral measurements.
NASA HRP · HFBP · NTRS · Artemis research
Scope rule: spaceflight evidence tests cognition, physiology, and operational state.
It is not cited as evidence for a specific physical-to-experiential bridge.
This separation makes the extreme-environment layer scientifically useful without overstating the source role.
